claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help determine your eligibility, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for. 

**First, let me ask: How old is the child (or children) you're inquiring about?**

For Child Benefit eligibility, the child's age is important:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualifying
- **16-19**: Qualifying if in education or approved training
- **20 or over**: Generally not qualifying

Please tell me the name(s) and age(s) of the child/children you're claiming for.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit. 

I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have **Alex, who is 17 years old**.

Since Alex is 17, they fall into the 16-19 age category. For this age group, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether Alex is in education or approved training.

**Can you tell me: Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?**

For example:
- Full-time school or college
- A full-time course at university
- An approved apprenticeship or training scheme
- Or is Alex working full-time instead?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in college doing A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for clarifying that Alex is in college doing A-levels - that's full-time education.

Let me navigate through the eligibility requirements for this situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me continue - since Alex is in full-time education (A-levels at college), I'll navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! Alex is studying A-levels, which is **approved non-advanced education** - this is exactly what qualifies for Child Benefit at age 17.

However, I need to check one more important thing: **Is Alex working full-time while doing A-levels, or is Alex not working full-time?**

This is important because even though Alex is in approved education, if they're working full-time (in addition to or instead of their studies), they wouldn't qualify.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working full-time - just focusing on the studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's great. Since Alex is not working full-time and is focusing on their studies, let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Since Alex is not working full-time and is just focusing on studies, let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

Most students wouldn't be receiving these, but I need to confirm for completeness.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't receiving any benefits like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check: **Is Alex in an apprenticeship programme?**

Since Alex is doing A-levels at college, they're likely not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship - just the A-levels at college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is not in an apprenticeship and is just doing A-levels at college, let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. **Do you (the claimant) normally live in the UK?**

This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility. Child Benefit is generally available to people who normally live in the UK. There are some special circumstances if you have settled/pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme or are a Crown servant living abroad, but the main requirement is UK residency.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since you normally live in the UK, let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm: **Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means either:
- You live with Alex, OR
- You're contributing to their upkeep (paying for food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.), OR
- You're making maintenance payments under a court order or agreement

Which applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex lives with you at home, you are responsible for them. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else claimed for Alex?**

For example, is Alex's other parent (if applicable) also claiming Child Benefit for them?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Since no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's current living situation: **Is Alex living at home normally, or is there anything special about their current situation?**

For example:
- Is Alex in hospital?
- Is Alex in residential care?
- Is Alex fostered?
- Or is Alex living with you at home normally?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living at home with me normally - nothing special about the situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! One final question: **Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, the council is not contributing financially to support Alex's living costs at home - this is usually the case for most families, but I need to confirm for completeness.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me navigate to the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me provide you with your final eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You are **ELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit

---

### Your Eligibility Result for Alex

**Status:** ✅ **ELIGIBLE**

**Summary:** You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex. As a 17-year-old in full-time approved education (A-levels), living with you at home in the UK with no other claimants, Alex qualifies for Child Benefit.

---

### Key Reasons for Eligibility:
1. ✅ Alex is 17 years old and in approved full-time education (A-levels)
2. ✅ Alex is not working full-time
3. ✅ Alex is not receiving disqualifying benefits
4. ✅ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
5. ✅ You normally live in the UK
6. ✅ You are responsible for Alex (living together)
7. ✅ No one else is claiming for Alex
8. ✅ The council is not paying towards Alex's support

---

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of:**
   - Your identity
   - Alex's identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate

3. **Important - High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may have to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through tax (the High Income Child Benefit Charge)

4. **Payment Schedule:**
   - Payments are made every 4 weeks, or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits

---

**For more information, visit:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or your eligibility?
